clue.text: Blow up tyre after journey

indicators.note: after places the tyre word behind the journey word in the answer

parts.note: to go is to make a journey
a spare is a reserve tyre carried in a car

explanation.surface: A motorist's tyre bursts after a long drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' looks like the tyre bursting, but it is the definition: to go spare is British slang for losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal idioms for flying into a sudden furious rage.

clue.text: Craftsman less inclined to work hard after good start

indicators.note: after puts the idler word behind the letter from good
the start of the word good is its opening letter

parts.note: lazier means more idle, less keen on toil

explanation.surface: A tradesman who has grown idle after a promising beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier is a skilled tradesman who cuts and fits window glass.

clue.text: A good turn, supplying spectacles and hat

parts.note: spectacles here are shows or displays, not glasses
a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: Someone does a kindness by handing over glasses and a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectacles' wants to mean eyeglasses; it means shows. 'A good turn' is not a favour but a stage act so good it halts the performance.
explanation.definitionFit: In variety theatre a turn is an act, and a showstopper is one so good the applause stops proceedings.

clue.text: Man is at the bottom of a very loud quarrel

indicators.note: in a down clue being at the bottom means coming after the other pieces

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
Ray is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man ends up at the centre of a noisy row.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public brawl or fight, a violent quarrel in legal language.

clue.text: More than a side written in this exam?

definitions.text: More than a side written in this exam?

parts.words: More than a side written in this exam?
parts.note: a cricket or football side has eleven players, so more than a side is that number plus; the joke pretends candidates write over a page

explanation.walkthrough: A side is a team of eleven, and 'side' also suggests a page of writing. The British exam once taken at about age eleven to decide grammar-school entry is named for that age.
explanation.definitionFit: The test sat by British pupils at age eleven or over is named after that age.

clue.text: Motorcyclists, note, joining in squabbles

indicators.note: joining in says the note goes inside the motorcyclists

parts.note: bikers ride motorcycles
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A biker gang argues, with a musician tagging along.
explanation.definitionFit: To bicker is to squabble over petty things, so both are verbs for petty arguing.

clue.text: Sense of excitement resulting from phone call

definitions.meaning: a thrill or rush of excitement
informal: give someone a ring on the telephone

explanation.surface: Getting thrilled after a phone rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzz is both a thrill and, colloquially, a telephone call: give me a buzz.

clue.text: Love one in France, freshly-brewed?.

indicators.note: brewing stirs things up, so these letters are made afresh in a new order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone adores a hot drink just made on a trip to France.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints a stray full stop after the question mark. The whole clue also describes the answer: French black coffee, newly brewed.
explanation.definitionFit: Café noir is the French phrase for black coffee, the drink one would love in France.

clue.text: Letter from abroad, and when it's due?

definitions.meaning: a letter of the Greek alphabet
estimated time of arrival, when a flight or train is expected

explanation.surface: Waiting for a letter posted overseas and wondering when it will arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh Greek letter, and ETA stands for estimated time of arrival.

clue.text: Writer is to show, delight over novel being at the top

indicators.note: in a down entry being at the top means placed first

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: over in a down clue turns the word upside down, so it reads upwards

parts.note: to yell is to show delight noisily

explanation.surface: An author must express joy that his novel tops the charts.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' turns the delight word upwards to LLEY. 'is to' is a link; the novel is H. Rider Haggard's adventure story.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe Shelley and Mary Shelley were both celebrated English writers.

clue.text: Characters regularly seen in Bangkok in the past

indicators.note: taking characters at regular intervals means every other letter of the city name

explanation.surface: Letters spotted on signs during a past visit to Thailand's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth and sixth letters of Bangkok.
explanation.definitionFit: Ago is an adverb placing something earlier in time, as in years ago.

clue.text: Still, hardly a hotshot?

definitions.meaning: a single frozen picture from a film
a shot that is freezing is the opposite of a hot one, playing on frame as a shot

explanation.surface: A photographer who is still not much of an ace.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeze-frame is a single motionless image held from a film, like a still.

clue.text: Extremely trendy suit

parts.note: in means fashionable
spades is a suit of playing cards

explanation.surface: A very fashionable outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing; it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom meaning in large measure or to a great degree, used as an adverb like extremely.

clue.text: A certain problem for a playwright

parts.note: one can mean a certain, as in one Mr Smith
an ill is a problem or trouble

explanation.surface: A dramatist faces a particular difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill was an American dramatist, author of Long Day's Journey into Night.

clue.text: Spanish girl's competent, it's unlikely to be denied

parts.note: Ines is a Spanish girl's name; the 's is a link
capable means competent

explanation.surface: A Spanish woman is so able that she is hard to refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inescapable cannot be avoided or denied.

clue.text: Europeans a bit different? Very much so

parts.note: Poles are natives of Poland
a part is a bit or portion

explanation.surface: Asking whether some Europeans are slightly unusual, and getting a firm yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different? Very much so' together means extremely different.
explanation.definitionFit: Things poles apart are as far removed from each other as possible, entirely different.

clue.text: Cross land area

definitions.meaning: a crucifix, especially one in a church
an old unit of land, a quarter of an acre

explanation.surface: Crossing a plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix above a church screen and also an old measure of land.

clue.text: A pupil initially secured place in college, as is fitting

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of pupil
secured says the place is held inside the college
in confirms the place goes within the college

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a kind of college
a site is a place

explanation.surface: A student, at first, got a place at college, quite properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secured ... in' both signal the container: the college holds the place. A poly was a British polytechnic, a college awarding degrees until 1992.
explanation.definitionFit: Appositely means suitably or aptly, in a way that is fitting.

clue.text: Prisoner keeps saying name

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the prisoner word wraps the other

parts.note: a con is a convict
a gnome is a maxim or aphorism

explanation.surface: A jailbird keeps repeating someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: GNOME in the sense of a pithy saying is a less familiar meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A cognomen is a name, originally the third or family name of a Roman citizen.

clue.text: Agent scoured fresh copies

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative or agent

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sales agent scrubbed some new items clean.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs: to reproduce something is to make copies of it.

clue.text: Classified differently: that's noted down right away

indicators.note: away says the letter for right is removed

parts.note: recorded means noted down

explanation.surface: Something reclassified, and it is written down immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like immediately; it means remove R. 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To recode is to classify again under a different system of codes.

clue.text: Lover of Galatea, racist at heart

indicators.note: at heart means the letters come from the inside of the word

explanation.surface: Galatea's lover is revealed to be a bigot deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle four letters of racist.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Acis was the shepherd loved by the nymph Galatea.

clue.text: Dexterity of extremely skilful rowing crew

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: an eight is a racing boat crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: The deftness of a very skilled crew in a boat race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like 'very'; it takes S and L, the first and last letters of skilful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means skill or dexterity, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Barrister collapsed, wearily, having lost one

indicators.note: collapsed suggests a falling down, so the letters are rearranged
having lost says a piece is missing from the rearranged pool

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A barrister fell down from tiredness, having lost a case.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I from WEARILY and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister is a type of lawyer who argues cases in court.

clue.text: Showing concern about group operating illegally

parts.note: ca, circa, means about
a ring is a gang of criminals

explanation.surface: Concern shown over a criminal gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Caring is an adjective meaning showing kindness and concern for others.

clue.text: Fruit tree's bark protected

indicators.note: protected means kept within, so the tree word holds the bark

parts.note: the maple is a tree; the 's is a link
to yap is to bark shrilly

explanation.surface: A fruit tree's bark is covered for protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bark' looks like tree covering; it is a dog's yap.
explanation.definitionFit: The mayapple is a North American woodland plant bearing an edible yellow fruit.

clue.text: Head boy's first to go, in bygone era

indicators.note: to go means that letter is removed

parts.note: bonce is British slang for the head

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of boy

explanation.surface: A head boy must be the first to leave, as in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head boy' reads as the school title; split it. BONCE is British slang for head.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at a former time, formerly, long ago.

clue.text: TV programme made country uneasy

indicators.note: uneasy suggests a disturbed state, so these letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: A television show unsettled the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A documentary is a factual programme on television.

clue.text: Modest group 'of soldiers

definitions.meaning: .... is the abbreviation for company, a military unit

explanation.surface: A shy unit of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The page shows a stray apostrophe before 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coy means bashfully modest, and Coy is short for company, a body of soldiers.

clue.text: Seize item of luggage

explanation.surface: Grab a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: To bag is to seize or capture, and a bag is an item of luggage.

clue.text: Old lady swindled out of money abroad

indicators.note: the swindled word sits outside the money

parts.note: done is slang for cheated
the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: An elderly woman cheated of her cash on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected senior woman in a field, a grande dame.

clue.text: Suffering old marines to enter shelter

indicators.note: to enter means go inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Veteran marines suffer as they go into a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment means extreme suffering, either physical or mental.
